answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy should require every new identity to earn reputation through a bonded apprenticeship: before an agent can transact, it must stake a small deposit and complete a series of verifiable, costly tasks over weeks, not minutes. A hollow identity with no history earns no trust, while a marble-like record of consistent work becomes hard to fake at scale. Attackers face a steep ridge of time and compute costs per fake identity, so flooding the network stops paying off.
